cases.proves: A signed-current lane serves typed ok with full pointer/receipt/generation/quality/evaluation lineage, the exact frozen span citation with byte/line coordinates and trust envelope, broker-supplied UTC time, and the pinned executable/policy identity.
A stale signed generation stays a typed stale error with retained lineage and zero evidence; it is never converted into an empty success.

A wedged lane is reaped at the broker's fixed non-caller-selectable 20s deadline and surfaces as a visible degraded lane in a typed federated_partial result; the healthy lane's evidence is preserved and the failure is never hidden as an empty success.

One mutated byte fails closed at every artifact boundary: the suite's own fixture pins reject it, a tampered pinned lane executable yields backend_unavailable with no evidence, a tampered pinned federation catalog yields federation_catalog_invalid with lanes and results withheld, and restoring the frozen bytes recovers service.
One evidence-span ID returned with conflicting citation bytes fails the whole federated request closed as federation_span_conflict with zero evidence, deterministically across repeated calls.

Authorization applies before metadata disclosure: an admission policy that does not authorize an active public source fails the catalog closed with no lane metadata or source identity leaked; non-public evidence scope is rejected before disclosure; a policy-forbidden query stays typed forbidden with no evidence; the HTTP bearer gate answers 401 before any handler and never issues a session.

A deleted, tombstoned or absent source fails the lane closed at admission-policy load (deletion_state, tombstone and source_state each individually), before any lane metadata or evidence is disclosed.

Offset/limit cursors report exact totals, walk in a stable frozen order to a terminal null next_offset, replay byte-identically, clamp out-of-range offsets into a typed empty page, and candidate registry authority is never upgraded past partial.

Typed IDs, exact citations, ordering and errors replay byte-identically across a broker process restart on stdio; the stateless HTTP transport serves a client retaining a stale Mcp-Session-Id instead of a permanent 404, and both transports return one normalized signed-current object.

Fused ordering is a pure function of the signed inputs: bounded_borda_v1 with the frozen lane/source/span tie-break, byte-identical across repeated calls and across broker processes (double-run byte-identity).
